title: Sources of Indian History
subject: History (CDS/NDA)

blocks.heading: 🏛️ Sources of Indian History
blocks.intro: Historians reconstruct the past using two primary categories of sources: Archaeological and Literary.

blocks.heading: 1. Archaeological Sources (High-Yield)
bullets: Inscriptions (Epigraphy): The most reliable source. Ashokan Edicts: Written in Brahmi, Kharosthi, Greek, and Aramaic scripts. Deciphered by **James Prinsep** in 1837.
Allahabad Pillar Inscription (Prasasti): Composed in Sanskrit by Harishena, praising Gupta King Samudragupta.
Aihole Inscription: Written by Ravikirti, describing Chalukya King Pulakeshin II's victory over Harsha.
Uttaramerur Inscription: Details the self-governing village administration of the Imperial Cholas.
Coins (Numismatics): Tell us about economic health, trade relations, and kingly interests. Punch-marked coins (silver/copper) were the earliest.
**Indo-Greeks** were the first to issue coins with portraits and legends.
**Kushanas** issued the first large-scale gold coins in India.
**Guptas** issued the largest number of gold coins (Dinars). Samudragupta's coins show him playing the Veena.

blocks.heading: 2. Literary Sources
bullets: Religious Texts: Vedas, Puranas, Epics (Ramayana, Mahabharata), Buddhist Tripitakas (Pali), and Jain Angas (Prakrit).
Secular Literature: Kautilya's Arthashastra (statecraft and administration).
Kalhana's Rajatarangini (12th century, history of Kashmir, India's first scientific historical work).
Foreign Accounts: **Greek:** Megasthenes ( Indica , Mauryan administration).
**Chinese:** Fa-Hien (Gupta period under Chandragupta II) and Hiuen Tsang (Harsha's reign, studied at Nalanda).
**Arab/Persian:** Al-Biruni ( Kitab-ul-Hind , 11th century culture and science), Ibn Battuta ( Rihla , Tughlaq period).

formulas: Epigraphy: Inscriptions | Numismatics: Coins | Rajatarangini: Kalhana (Kashmir history)
